front: Six blocks of a forecasting platform?
back: Data contracts, feature and calendar layer, model registry, backtest service, training and serving, monitoring and governance.

front: What does a model registry guarantee?
back: Versioned models with code, data snapshot and parameters, so any past forecast can be reproduced.
Self-serve: team owns pipeline. Managed: platform runs it from a config. Embedded: a platform engineer joins the team for a time.
It uses the same folds and metrics for all teams, so accuracy numbers are comparable.

front: Why use shadow mode when migrating?
back: It compares new and old forecasts on live data without risk, and shows if the new one is at least as good.
Mostly for organisational reasons: no owner, forced one-size models, no adoption plan, no clear success metric.
